title: How to Take on The Epstein Class and the Billionaire Elites with Katie Phang
text:
Katie Phang isn’t stupid. She knows she’s trying to uncover the biggest political cover-up in modern history orchestrated by a powerful, transnational criminal syndicate that includes Presidents, world leaders, billionaires, and financial institutions.
Still, that doesn’t mean you don’t fight for accountability and justice.
Phang, who is an attorney and former cable news host, has sued acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to comply with the Epstein Transparency Act. She wants answers, and she wants the files that the Trump Administration is covering up because it directly implicates Donald Trump, a rapist and a convicted criminal. Thankfully, Judge Sullivan also wants answers and has ruled that Blanche has until Thursday to turn over unredacted files.
Will he?
Probably not, but that doesn’t mean he’s not feeling the pressure. Blanche, Trump, and Republicans are slowly being backed into a corner because a majority of Americans, including their base, demand answers. They were promised the Epstein Files. Where are they? Why are they being hidden? Who is being protected?
Another angle Phang is exploring is the incestuous “modeling agency” world that connects all these players, including Daniel Said, who was found dead last week, because of course. Let’s remember Melania Trump was once a model and was allegedly introduced to Donald by agent Paolo Zampolli, who is also connected to Jeffrey Epstein. There’s also the suicide of Jean-Luc Brunel, the French modeling agent who was complicit in the Epstein sex trafficking ring.
It’s all a big club that is desperately trying to protect itself from accountability. This big club includes billionaires such as Larry and David Ellison who have purchased Paramount and now want to merge with Warner Bros. That will give them control of two major Hollywood studios, CBS News, HBO, and CNN. Larry Ellison has already gobbled up TikTok. Thankfully, due to non-stop outrage and coverage, that merger has been delayed by a year.
Again, fighting the good fight matters and we can still have nice things, provided enough people care.
Katie Phang joins me to break down both stories.
